seeds.text: An old woman sells maps of places that do not exist yet.
It is not a cult. It is a family.
A key ally is sick and cannot be moved.
A glass bottle holding a captured sunrise.
Knows far too much about the heroes.

concept.title: Twenty Years in the Dark
concept.tagline: Follow Mads down through Tarnmoor, find the logbook in the lower halls and bring it out before the gate is walled up at dawn.
concept.teaser: Ivar Fellmere seeks out the heroes late in the evening, the water-stained page in hand, and begs them to go down after Mads and bring the rest of the logbook up before the gate is walled up.
concept.premise: Twenty years ago Mads came up alone from Tarnmoor and told Crookcombe that the rest of the survey party had died when a vault fell in. It was a lie: Mads wedged the door to the lower halls shut behind the others and walked off with the silver they had found together. Now Ivar Fellmere, whose mother led the party, has found a page of her logbook in the junk that goblins and orcs drag out of Tarnmoor. Mads, head of the council these days, has ordered the gate walled up at dawn and has gone down alone tonight to burn the rest of the logbook.
concept.goal: Follow Mads down through Tarnmoor, find the logbook in the lower halls and bring it out before the gate is walled up at dawn.

objective.target: The survey party’s logbook, kept by Ivar Fellmere’s mother to her last day
objective.state: In a tin box in the deepest hall behind the wedged door, where the orc (warrior veteran) now lairs. Mads is searching for it with lamp oil and a tinderbox.
objective.resolution: Get the box past the orc (warrior veteran) and Mads, and carry it out through the gate or the old crawlway before dawn. If the heroes cannot, they must save what pages they can, and it becomes their word against Mads’s. By force: defeat the orc (warrior veteran) and the others or break through (a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check; a door or chain has AC 15 and 18 HP). On a failure, 10 minutes pass and the noise wakes the rest of the place. Without a fight: draw the orc (warrior veteran) away from the farthest pillar with noise or fire while one hero sneaks in and takes the box (a DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) check). On a failure, the orc (warrior veteran) turns back too soon, and Mads gets a round to set the box alight.

concept.stakes: If the logbook burns or is walled in, the truth about the survey party is lost for good: Mads keeps the council and the silver, and Ivar Fellmere is branded a liar for asking.

clock.start: Late evening. The masons have stone and mortar stacked at the gate of Tarnmoor, and Mads went down an hour ago with a lamp, a crowbar and a flask of oil.

ticks.event: Mads has searched the party’s old camp in the middle halls in vain and burns everything left there.
ticks.sign: The smell of burnt leather and paper drifts up the stairs, and the soot in the camp is still warm.

ticks.event: Mads pries the wedged door open, and goblins and orcs from the lower halls spread up through Tarnmoor.
ticks.sign: A long shriek of iron on stone echoes through the halls, and goblins and orcs turn up in rooms the heroes have already cleared.

ticks.event: The masons wall up the gate, and Mads crawls out through the crawlway, leaving the logbook as ash.
ticks.sign: The light at the gate disappears stone by stone, and the scrape of trowels carries down the stairs.

clock.deadline: After 8 hours, at dawn, it is too late: the gate is walled up, the logbook is ash, and anyone still inside must find the crawlway or be shut in with goblins and orcs.
clock.costs: The scenes give the travel times, the shortcuts and how long a thorough search takes. A short rest takes 1 hour.

hooks: Ivar Fellmere seeks out the heroes late in the evening, the water-stained page in hand, and begs them to go down after Mads and bring the rest of the logbook up before the gate is walled up.
The temple sends the cleric to Crookcombe: Ivar Fellmere has asked for help, and the people there need someone who is neither afraid nor bought.
An old acquaintance whispers to the rogue that something is wrong in Crookcombe and that Ivar Fellmere is looking for people who can move quietly and keep their mouths shut.

villain.name: Mads
villain.nature: A council leader who came back alone from the survey party twenty years ago
villain.want: To keep the council seat, the good name and the fortune built on the stolen silver, and never be asked about those twenty years again.
villain.plan: First, Mads had the council order the gate walled up so that goblins and orcs cannot get out. Tonight Mads burns everything in the party’s old camp and pries the wedged door open to reach the deepest hall. At dawn Mads slips out through the old crawlway while the masons seal the gate behind the evidence.
villain.weakness: Mads has not set foot in Tarnmoor for twenty years, is terrified of the dark and is counting on the old crawlway as a way out. Whoever finds it on Mads’s old map can wait at its far end, or block it.

cast.name: Ivar Fellmere
cast.role: A child of the lost survey leader

cast.name: Ravn
cast.role: A master mason ordered to wall up the gate at dawn

cast.name: Brynja
cast.role: A silversmith who still has one of Mads’s old silver ingots

outline.title: The Water-Stained Page
outline.purpose: Late in the evening Ivar Fellmere seeks out the heroes with a page of the survey party’s logbook in hand: it is written by Ivar’s mother, and its last entry names Mads. Ivar begs them to go down into Tarnmoor after Mads and bring the rest of the logbook up before the gate is walled up at dawn. The town can give more answers before they go, but every visit costs time that Mads spends below.

outline.title: The Oil Trail on the Stair
outline.purpose: Beyond the gate lie the upper halls, where goblins and orcs have dragged junk together in heaps. Fresh drips of lamp oil and the prints of good town boots lead past every side passage and straight down, while the party’s old chalk arrows take a longer way to the same place. The scene shows that Mads knows the way, and that the party once walked it too.

outline.title: The Burnt Camp
outline.purpose: In the middle halls lies the survey party’s old camp, where the party lived before going down behind the door. Mads has burnt everything left there, but under a half-burnt chest lies a charred scrap that tells where the logbook is. If the heroes get there by the first tick, they see the fire being lit.

outline.title: The Wedged Door
outline.purpose: The door to the lower halls was wedged shut from the outside twenty years ago, with the party on the other side. After the second tick Mads has pried it open and goblins and orcs from the lower halls are pouring up through the passages; if the heroes get here sooner, Mads is still at work with the crowbar. Here it becomes plain that no vault fell: the party was shut in.

outline.title: The Hall of Seven Pillars
outline.purpose: The deepest hall is the orc’s lair now, and here lies the party’s last camp: bones in rotted cloaks, and the tin box with the logbook beside the leader. Mads is here with oil and a tinderbox to burn the logbook and then slip out through the crawlway, but the orc (warrior veteran) serves no one and attacks whatever disturbs the hall. The heroes must get the box out before it burns, and decide whether Mads gets away.

outline.title: The Aftermath
outline.purpose: The logbook is read aloud in the council hall, and Mads is led out in dead silence. The silver goes to the families of the lost, and Ivar Fellmere asks the heroes to guide the party that will bring the dead home from the deepest hall.

clues.observation: The page Ivar Fellmere found: water-stained, written in a firm hand, its last entry naming Mads.
clues.inference: Mads wedged the door and took the silver; the story of the fallen vault is a lie.
clues.handout:
Day 9. The door will not give. Mads is on the other side and does not answer.
The silver sledge is gone, and the rope with it.
We have water for four days. I will keep writing.

clues.observation: The council stores ledger shows an entry from yesterday in Mads’s own hand: a crowbar, two lanterns and a flask of lamp oil.
clues.inference: Mads meant to go down in person, and with oil, not mortar.
clues.handout:
Issued from the council stores:
1 crowbar, 2 hooded lanterns, 1 flask of lamp oil.
Purpose: inspection of Tarnmoor before sealing. — Mads

clues.observation: Brynja, the silversmith, still has an ingot Mads sold twenty years ago. It is stamped with the survey party’s mark, a compass rose.
clues.inference: Mads came up with the party’s silver, not empty-handed as the story goes.

clues.observation: Chalk arrows marked with a little compass rose, the party’s old sign, point down through the halls toward the wedged door.
clues.inference: The party fell back behind the door to the deepest hall; the logbook must be there.

clues.observation: In Mads’s desk at the council hall lies the old survey map, drawn in Mads’s own hand.
clues.inference: The deepest hall has a second way out that the official report never mentions, and that is the one Mads means to use.
clues.handout:
Lower halls: the silver lies in the deepest hall (seven pillars).
Crawlway from the deepest hall comes out 300 paces east of the gate.
Not to be shown to the council.

clues.observation: Fresh drips of lamp oil and the prints of good town boots lead past every side passage and straight down.
clues.inference: Mads knows the way and is heading for the deepest hall.

partyMoments.moment: The heroes snatch the box from Mads or out of the flames before the fire takes the pages (scene 5, “The Hall of Seven Pillars”: Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), DC 13).
The climax (scene 5, “The Hall of Seven Pillars”): healing that keeps the others on their feet.

In Mads’s desk the heroes find the old survey map and now know that the deepest hall has a second way out, 300 paces east of the gate (scene 1, “The Water-Stained Page”: Intelligence (Investigation), DC 13).
The heroes hold the doorway so that only a few goblins and orcs can reach them at a time, and the fight gets easier (scene 4, “The Wedged Door”: Strength (Athletics), DC 13).

scenes.title: The Water-Stained Page
scenes.summary: Late in the evening Ivar Fellmere seeks out the heroes with a page of the survey party’s logbook in hand: it is written by Ivar’s mother, and its last entry names Mads. Ivar begs them to go down into Tarnmoor after Mads and bring the rest of the logbook up before the gate is walled up at dawn. The town can give more answers before they go, but every visit costs time that Mads spends below.
scenes.readAloud: The inn is about to close when a figure in a damp cloak walks straight to your table and smooths a page out between the mugs. The paper is water-stained and brittle at the edges, and the handwriting is firm and neat. Through the open door a cart loaded with sacks of mortar rumbles past on its way to the gate of Tarnmoor.
details: Ivar Fellmere found the page in the junk that goblins and orcs drag out of Tarnmoor and showed it around town. The next morning Mads signed the order to wall up the gate, and at nightfall Ivar watched Mads walk out to the gate alone with a lamp and a crowbar.

Three places in town each cost a half-hour detour: the council stores, where the ledger shows what Mads took out yesterday; Brynja, the silversmith, who has an ingot stamped with the party’s compass rose; and Mads’s desk in the council hall, holding the old survey map, the only thing that shows the crawlway. Ravn, the master mason, sits with the order at the gate, which the heroes must pass anyway.

Getting there: from Crookcombe to the gate, half an hour; through the upper halls, half an hour; to the party’s camp in the middle halls, 1 hour by the oil trail or 1½ hours by the chalk arrows; from there, half an hour to the wedged door and half an hour more to the hall of seven pillars. Without detours the heroes stand at the door after 2½ hours, just before Mads breaks it open; every stop in town or in the halls adds to that.

Mads has an hour’s lead, but spends an hour rummaging through the party’s old camp for the logbook and only sets it alight at the first tick. Only a group that goes straight down can get there while the fire is being lit.

checks.success: Ravn shows the order, lets the heroes in without raising the alarm and promises to send word down the stair before the last stone is set.
checks.failure: Ravn sticks to the order that no one may go in; the heroes must wait until the masons leave their fire, or sneak past, and that costs half an hour.

checks.success: In Mads’s desk the heroes find the old survey map and now know that the deepest hall has a second way out, 300 paces east of the gate.
checks.failure: The map lies under a false bottom in the drawer; the heroes find it, but only after another half hour of searching.

alternatives: Go straight down without detours: the heroes may reach the camp before it burns, but know nothing of the crawlway.
If the heroes have the map, Ivar Fellmere can go to the far end of the crawlway east of the gate and wait there with a few neighbours, so that Mads cannot slip out unseen.
scenes.dmNotes: Let the players choose between knowledge and time themselves. Say aloud what each visit costs, and let another mortar cart rumble past whenever they hesitate.

scenes.title: The Oil Trail on the Stair
scenes.summary: Beyond the gate lie the upper halls, where goblins and orcs have dragged junk together in heaps. Fresh drips of lamp oil and the prints of good town boots lead past every side passage and straight down, while the party’s old chalk arrows take a longer way to the same place. The scene shows that Mads knows the way, and that the party once walked it too.
scenes.readAloud: The stair beyond the gate is slick with damp, and every tenth step has a small, glossy spot that smells of lamp oil. In the hall below lie heaps of broken crates, rusty buckets and old blankets, dragged together and rummaged through. On a pillar a faded chalk arrow marked with a little compass rose points on down into the dark.
details: The heaps are the work of goblins and orcs, and some of them sleep in the junk at night. Among the heaps lie remains from the party’s time: a cracked lantern and a rusty measuring rod with the compass rose burned into it.

The oil trail goes straight down and saves half an hour; the chalk arrows follow the party’s old survey through the side passages. Both lead to the party’s camp in the middle halls, and from there on to the wedged door.

If the first tick has passed, the smell of burnt leather and paper drifts up the stair. After the second tick the wedged door is open, and goblins and orcs from the lower halls roam up here too, even in halls the heroes have already cleared.

checks.success: The boot prints are from tonight: one person, walking fast and keeping to the middle of the floor, as if afraid of the walls. The heroes follow the oil trail and save half an hour.
checks.failure: The heroes follow the chalk arrows instead, and the party’s old detour costs half an hour.

checks.success: The heroes get past the heaps without waking anything.
checks.failure: A bucket topples and some goblins and orcs wake. They follow at a distance and join in when the heroes reach the wedged door.

alternatives: Follow the chalk arrows on purpose: the detour costs time but comes out on a ledge above the party’s camp, so the heroes can see who is down there before they go in.
Put out food or something shiny by the heaps, so that goblins and orcs are busy squabbling over it while the heroes slip past.
scenes.dmNotes: Mention the oil drips every time the heroes choose which way to go. They are a thread for the players to hold on to, and a reminder that Mads is ahead of them.

scenes.title: The Burnt Camp
scenes.summary: In the middle halls lies the survey party’s old camp, where the party lived before going down behind the door. Mads has burnt everything left there, but under a half-burnt chest lies a charred scrap that tells where the logbook is. If the heroes get there by the first tick, they see the fire being lit.
scenes.readAloud: The hall reeks of burnt leather and lamp oil, and the soot on the walls is still warm. Bedrolls, a chest and a stack of papers have become a black, smoking heap in the middle of the floor. Along the wall stands a row of rusty water jugs, neatly lined up, as if someone expected to come back.
details: Under the chest, where the fire did not quite reach, lies a charred scrap that Mads missed: the leader took the box with the logbook into the hall of seven pillars.

If the heroes arrive by the first tick, Mads is standing in the middle of the camp, pouring oil over the bedrolls. At the sight of them Mads drops one of the lanterns, the fire catches, and Mads runs on down toward the wedged door. The heroes can chase Mads or save what lies in the flames, but not both.
The ash still glows beneath the surface, and the oil has made the floor slick. Anyone digging in the heap with bare hands gets burnt, and a careless step can set the oil alight again.

checks.success: The heroes work the scrap free from under the chest without harming it, and now know the logbook lies in the hall of seven pillars.
checks.failure: Half the scrap crumbles in their hands; only the words "seven pillars" can still be read.

alternatives: Skip the camp and follow the oil trail straight on: the heroes gain time, but without the scrap or the map they do not know which of the lower halls to search.
scenes.dmNotes: The camp is where the players understand that Mads did not come to keep goblins and orcs in but to burn the truth. Give them a moment with that before the clock drives them on.

scenes.title: The Wedged Door
scenes.summary: The door to the lower halls was wedged shut from the outside twenty years ago, with the party on the other side. After the second tick Mads has pried it open and orcs from the lower halls are pouring up through the passages; if the heroes get here sooner, Mads is still at work with the crowbar. Here it becomes plain that no vault fell: the party was shut in.
scenes.readAloud: The passage ends at a heavy oak door bound with iron. Iron wedges, driven in from the outside and rusted by twenty years, line the frame, and across them run fresh, bright scratches from a crowbar. Cold air seeps out under the door, smelling of old dust, and something is moving on the other side.
details: Before the second tick Mads stands here with the lantern and the crowbar, the door almost open. At the sight of the heroes Mads tears the last wedge loose in a panic: the door gives with a shriek of iron on stone, orcs pour out between them, and Mads slips into the dark beyond.
After the second tick the door stands open, the wedges lie bent on the floor, and orcs from the lower halls are roaming up through Tarnmoor; the heroes meet them in the doorway.

The inside of the door is covered in scratches at shoulder height and a few words cut with a knife: the party’s names and a date several days after the day Mads came up and told of the fallen vault. Under the door is a gap just wide enough for a sheet of paper; this is where the leader pushed out the page that Ivar Fellmere found.

checks.success: The heroes make out the words inside the door: the party was alive for days after the day Mads said they died. It is proof the council can see with its own eyes.
checks.failure: The scratches are too worn to read by lantern light, but the heroes can copy them and have them read later.

checks.success: The heroes hold the doorway so that only a few orcs can reach them at a time, and the fight gets easier.
checks.failure: The heroes are pushed back into the passage and orcs come at them from several sides; the fight is harder, but afterwards the way through the door is open.

alternatives: Hide in a side passage and let Mads do the work: when the door gives, orcs rush up past the hiding place, and the heroes can follow Mads’s lantern into the dark.
Lure orcs away with noise or a thrown light, and slip through the door while they search.
scenes.dmNotes: Use the timing. If the heroes arrive before the second tick, let the door give way in front of them; if they come later, the fight has already spread through the passages and Mads has a long lead.

scenes.title: The Hall of Seven Pillars
scenes.summary: The deepest hall is the orc’s lair now, and here lies the party’s last camp: bones in rotted cloaks, and the tin box with the logbook beside the leader. Mads is here with oil and a tinderbox to burn the logbook and then slip out through the crawlway, but the orc (warrior veteran) serves no one and attacks whatever disturbs the hall. The heroes must get the box out before it burns, and decide whether Mads gets away.
scenes.readAloud: Seven pillars rise into the dark, and the light reaches only the first three. Between them lie the remains of a camp: rope, dried-out water skins and bones still wrapped in rotted cloaks. Far inside, a lantern stands on the floor by the farthest pillar, and a figure in a fine council cloak bends over a small tin box, a flask in hand.
details: If Mads is here, Mads does not fight (stat block: noble). Should the fight go badly, Mads tries to bargain or flee and, if cornered, would rather surrender than die.

The orc (warrior veteran) and some goblins lair here and do not serve Mads, who crept past them in the dark and is as afraid of them as of the heroes. When the fight begins, the orc (warrior veteran) goes for whoever is nearest, and Mads uses the noise to set the box alight or run for the crawlway.

The crawlway starts as a low crack behind the farthest pillar and comes out 300 paces east of the gate. The party never found it in the dark, but it is on Mads’s old map. If it is blocked, or someone waits at its far end, Mads has no way out and would rather surrender than be left alone in the dark.

The vault above the hall is intact; nothing ever fell in here. If the heroes are far behind Mads, the first pages are already burning as they come in, and they have one round to save the rest. At dawn the scrape of trowels carries down the stairs, and from then on the crawlway is the only way out.
Among the bones of the survey party’s last camp lies one more thing: a glass bottle holding a captured sunrise.

checks.success: The heroes snatch the box from Mads or out of the flames before the fire takes the pages.
checks.failure: The heroes get the box, but the outer pages are burnt; the last entries can still be read.

checks.success: Mads drops the oil flask and would rather surrender to the heroes than be left alone in the dark with the orc (warrior veteran).
checks.failure: Mads strikes a spark and runs for the crawlway; the box lands in the oil, and the heroes must choose between it and Mads.

alternatives: Block the crawlway first if the heroes know of it from the map: with no way out, Mads bargains for light and an escort up to the gate, and hands over the box.
Use noise or fire to draw the orc (warrior veteran) away from the farthest pillar while one hero sneaks in and takes the box.
scenes.dmNotes: Play Mads’s fear: down here Mads is not the head of the council, only someone afraid of the dark. Every clue the heroes found can be used here, above all the map with the crawlway.

scenes.title: The Aftermath
scenes.summary: The logbook is read aloud in the council hall, and Mads is led out in dead silence. The silver goes to the families of the lost, and Ivar Fellmere asks the heroes to guide the party that will bring the dead home from the deepest hall.
scenes.readAloud: Grey daylight falls on the gate of Tarnmoor, where the masons stand with their mortar, waiting for word. Over in Crookcombe the council gathers in the council hall, and every eye turns to those who come up from the deep.
details: If the heroes only partly succeed: The heroes come out with a few scorched pages but not the whole logbook, and Mads escapes through the crawlway. The town splits between those who believe the pages and those who believe the head of the council, and Mads starts buying the doubters back.

If the heroes fail: At dawn the gate is walled up, the logbook is ash, and Mads walks into Crookcombe as the one who shut the danger in just in time. Ivar Fellmere is fined for slander and leaves town, and before long goblins and orcs begin to find other ways out of Tarnmoor.
scenes.dmNotes: Narrate the ending that matches what the heroes actually achieved: if they succeeded, the summary holds; if not, one of the other two endings does. Then let each player say what their hero does next.

encounter.tactics: They fight while they outnumber the heroes and fall back once half of them are down.

treasure: A blood-red garnet cut like a drop

locations.name: The Gatehouse of the Half-Raised Portcullis
locations.readAloud: The sconces hold fresh torches that have never been lit. The floor tiles rock slightly underfoot and click back into place.
locations.description: A stack of plates on the table is glued together; beneath the bottom one lies a folded map.
features: A painting of this very place shows a door that does not exist in reality.
A tall bookcase topples if the wrong book is pulled, but the right one opens a gap behind it.

encounter.tactics: The strongest leads and the others follow. They fight while they outnumber the heroes and fall back once half of them are down.

locations.secret: Behind the fireplace is a pivoting door that opens when the third brick from the left is pulled.

locations.name: The Map Room of the Slashed World
locations.readAloud: The dust on the floor is swept into long arcs, as if something dragged a cloak behind it. Water drips from the ceiling in a slow rhythm.
locations.description: An iron ring in the floor is set in a heavy trapdoor that takes two people at once to lift.
features: A hoist with a basket hangs in a shaft, and the rope holds one person at a time.
A slate is covered in chalk marks counting days, and the last mark was made yesterday.

locations.name: The Chapel of Bricked-Up Windows
locations.readAloud: The wall paintings have been scraped away at exactly eye level. A clock ticks somewhere, unevenly, like the steps of someone with a limp.
locations.description: A suit of armour stands on a rack with its visor shut; inside, a bird has built a nest holding three eggs.
features: A huge cauldron hangs over a burnt-out fire; at the bottom, a handful of coins has melted into a lump.
In a row of cells, one door is locked from the inside.
treasure: A black pearl from an oyster nobody could open
locations.secret: The passage carries voices from a room further in, and anyone standing in the corner can hear everything said in there.

locations.name: The Dining Hall Still Laid for Supper
locations.readAloud: The cobwebs are torn through at knee height all the way down the passage. It smells of iron filings, as if someone sharpened blades here not long ago.
locations.description: A board game sits mid-match; moving the black queen slides out a drawer beneath the tabletop.
features: A white patch on the rock wall has been touched by a thousand hands and is smooth as soap.
A canvas is stretched under the ceiling; something heavy sags in it and shifts now and then.
treasure: A milk-white moonstone that turns bluish in the rain

locations.name: The Kennels of Gnawed Bars
locations.readAloud: The wall paintings have been scraped away at exactly eye level. It smells of cold tallow and stale incense.
locations.description: A rusty crank in the wall raises the portcullis, but only halfway.
features: A speaking tube in the wall leads somewhere; whisper into it, and after a while someone answers.
A row of small bells hangs from the ceiling on thin cords, and the slightest touch sets them all ringing.
treasure: A topaz that was once the eye of a statue

encounter.tactics: The orc (warrior veteran) leads the attack on the nearest hero, and the rest follow. Mads does not fight, keeps out of the way and tries to bargain once the fight turns.

treasure: A glass bottle holding a captured sunrise.

npcs.name: Mads
npcs.look: Is so pale that the veins show blue at the temples.
npcs.personality: Wildly enthusiastic about anything new, and forgets it just as fast.
npcs.wants: To keep the council seat, the good name and the fortune built on the stolen silver, and never be asked about those twenty years again.
npcs.secret: Mads has not set foot in Tarnmoor for twenty years, is terrified of the dark and is counting on the old crawlway as a way out. Whoever finds it on Mads’s old map can wait at its far end, or block it.
npcs.voice: Knows far too much about the heroes.

npcs.name: Ivar Fellmere
npcs.role: A child of the lost survey leader
npcs.look: Is weathered brown by sun and wind, with pale lines at the corners of their eyes where the sun never reached.
npcs.personality: Poor, but generous with what little there is.
npcs.wants: Wants their mother’s logbook read aloud in the council hall before the gate is walled up.
npcs.secret: Found the page last month but kept quiet, because Mads has paid for Ivar Fellmere’s apprenticeship ever since the survey party was lost.
npcs.voice: Talks to their animal instead of the heroes and lets the animal "answer".

npcs.name: Ravn
npcs.role: A master mason ordered to wall up the gate at dawn
npcs.look: Is unusually tall and always stoops as if the ceiling were too low, even outdoors.
npcs.personality: Afraid of the dark, but too embarrassed to say so.
npcs.wants: Wants the order confirmed by the whole council before the first stone is laid.
npcs.secret: Was paid an advance out of Mads’s own purse, not the council’s coffers, and has told no one.
npcs.voice: Hisses the s-sounds and smiles with a closed mouth.

npcs.name: Brynja
npcs.role: A silversmith who still has one of Mads’s old silver ingots
npcs.look: Has fingers full of rings, every one of them pewter.
npcs.personality: Nervous and painfully polite, especially to armed people.
npcs.wants: Wants to keep the workshop out of this, but will not lie to anyone.
npcs.secret: Bought not one ingot from Mads twenty years ago but twelve, and has always wondered about the compass rose.
npcs.voice: Speaks slowly and broadly, letting each word rest. Rubs their nose when a lie is on its way.

rewards.name: A black tourmaline that was a miner’s lucky stone
A walrus-ivory comb, a gift from a groom who never came to the wedding
The Silent Whistle
rewards.description: Only dogs and those who have blown it themselves can hear this whistle.

rewards.name: A glass bottle holding a captured sunrise
rewards.description: The real treasure of the adventure. It is worth more to the right people than to any merchant.

endings.success: The logbook is read aloud in the council hall, and Mads is led out in dead silence. The silver goes to the families of the lost, and Ivar Fellmere asks the heroes to guide the party that will bring the dead home from the deepest hall.
endings.partial: The heroes come out with a few scorched pages but not the whole logbook, and Mads escapes through the crawlway. The town splits between those who believe the pages and those who believe the head of the council, and Mads starts buying the doubters back.
endings.failure: At dawn the gate is walled up, the logbook is ash, and Mads walks into Crookcombe as the one who shut the danger in just in time. Ivar Fellmere is fined for slander and leaves town, and before long goblins and orcs begin to find other ways out of Tarnmoor.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes go back to Crookcombe for help.
unexpected.response: Give them help, but with strings attached: a guard who must come along, a councillor who wants the credit, or a price to be paid afterwards.
Have the absent player’s hero stay behind on an important task: guarding camp, following another lead or tending the wounded. The hero can return with news next time.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes are losing a fight they cannot win.
unexpected.response: Give the foes a reason to stop: they would rather take prisoners, an alarm draws them away, or their leader wants to bargain. Capture is a new scene, not an ending.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes try to buy their way out of trouble.
unexpected.response: Let the money work once, and let the price rise the next time. Anyone who takes a bribe can sell the heroes on, too.

unexpected.trigger: The heroes want to rest in the middle of enemy ground.
unexpected.response: Let them find an almost safe spot, and roll once for interruptions. The interruption can be a scout, an escaped prisoner or someone who wants to trade.

tips: Let the terrain join the fight: something that can be toppled, lit, climbed or pushed over.
If the group cannot agree on what to do, let time decide: something happens while they argue.
Do not ask for a roll if the result would change nothing.
Use the adventure’s names consistently. Write them on a card in front of you.
sequelHooks: Above Tarnmoor one star moves a little every night, and the astrologers of the capital are worried.
The king has heard of the heroes’ deed and sends word: there is a task only they can manage.
